Cut-cell current attribution — cumulative execution evidence

§1 — Root cause, found: the production current moments have not clipped a cell since 2026-08-27

Settled 2026-09-10, commit c9a89e58. The forward operator's profile support replaced traced_clip(signed_flux) with traced_clip(jnp.ones(...)) qualified by the profile participation label, so every cell has since been booked whole or not at all by which side of the separatrix its centroid falls on. What this explains, in order: 16 of 43 cut cells participating on the weak 110-cell row is the count whose centroids sit inside; the dominated error cells on single-null 110 are two-crossing cells booked whole (840.6 A against 85.6 A analytic); the four-crossing X-point cell is booked whole at 459.7 A against a 10.5 A core-side sliver; and on the transport machine 1072.71 A of scrape-off-layer current (0.19576 percent of Ip) is 844.30 A in sixteen separatrix-crossing cells plus 228.41 A in fifteen open cells carrying the edge-extrapolated profile. The full record with every panel lives at the cut-cell attribution evidence.

The three oracle gates — allocation, coupling, iteration

Gate A, allocation. On the exact input (analytic flux at the nodes) the global split spline books the analytic total to 1.00003 with zero boundary root error; the six-point ring quadratic books 0.99997 with a 0.15 mm median root error; the linear edge root falls 0.55 percent short (0.9945, 1.8 mm median root error) on weak, moderate and strong. The terminal-state shortfalls are state error (100 percent weak, 99.7 percent strong), and on the single-null 300 row every representation loses 20 percent at the terminal because the read admits no saddle and puts the boundary at the limiter, 21 percent of the span away — the §3 and null-identification census defect priced in current. Ship: the lead's locked choice of the global spline stands on its own number; the clip's linear edge root is the one representation with a measurable allocation error, so the consistent read (§4) replaces it.

Gate B, coupling. Gate B found a one to two percent smooth error when clipped first moments were imaged through the frozen linear-basis blocks; the held line rebuilt polygon-analytic blocks per trip, which changes the Biot geometry per trip — neither cacheable nor batchable nor differentiable. The lead's locked design is the frozen interaction matrix with the clipped current expanded to its moments about the atomic centroid (amplitude, gradient, curvature) to second order, imaged by matmul: a cached construction linear in cut cells, exact at the wall targets through the frozen Biot wall blocks.

Gate C, iteration. On the single-null 500 row under the fixture exterior, where the analytic flux is a fixed point to 4.9e-15, the production Newton-Krylov returned from perturbations of 1e-4 to 1e-1 of span to residual 6.2e-15 and distance 1.4e-14 from the analytic flux. Where the fixed point is the reference, the iteration contracts to it from a tenth of a span away; Gate C was never the iteration.

The reposed fixture exterior and the exact-clip memory findings

The fixture exterior is re-posed from the analytic density integrated over each cell's clipped region inside the analytic separatrix, cached with the machine. Gate at 1000 cells: exact-clip one-map floor 3.58e-5 of span on weak and 3.42e-5 on moderate (booked 0.99999) against 0.136 and 0.127 under the old whole-cell-integrated exterior; whole-cell booking now over-books 8.6 percent; single-null exact 0.109 at 500 and 0.045 at 1000 cells, apparent order 2.5 in pitch.

The exact-clip solve memory array is identified (H200 job 1270367, optimised HLO under docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/reposed-fixture/optimised-hlo). It is f64[cells, 196480, 6], 3.0 GiB per copy at 342 cells, repeated across the Newton JVP and transpose paths from fixed_point.py:3459: clipped_support_quadrature fans every cell's fixed-capacity support polygon into capacity-minus-two triangles and places a 64-point Gauss rule on each, and the exact clip's support capacity is 24 times 128 vertices, so 3070 triangles times 64 points equals 196480 quadrature points for every cell, whole cells included. In whole-cell mode the capacity is 24, the array is f64[342, 1408, 6] at 22 MiB and the program's temporaries total 0.19 GiB — 97 GiB against 0.19 GiB, so the exact-clip solve allocates 97, 131 and 279 GiB of booleans at 300, 500 and 1000 cells and fails even on an empty card. The fix is linear in cut cells: a chain capacity justified by the position accuracy the clip needs (a pitch over a thousand), the quadrature applied only to the cut cells at that capacity, and whole cells on the 24-vertex path.

Four fixed-capacity wedges in the single-null X-point cell

The analytic saddle, rather than the production null census, selects the cut cell by point-in-polygon. This distinction is decisive on the coarse meshes: the production census does not admit the saddle at 132 or 340 realised cells. At the requested 300-cell rung, the unique strict-containment candidate is realised cell 5. The saddle is interior and 6.500849 mm from its nearest edge. Four roots cross the boundary, but edge 2 carries two of them at fractions 0.2072052925 and 0.9283123862 despite same-sign endpoint samples. The endpoint-sign path therefore found only two roots and emitted an all-zero saddle row. This reproduced the recorded defect before the repair.

The repair accepts up to two ordered roots per edge, pairs the four roots cyclically by branch, and emits four polygons with a static capacity of 12 vertices. Every polygon begins with the analytic saddle; unused coordinates are bitwise zero. A saddle coincident with an edge root is represented by the same layout, leaving the repeated-root wedge with exact-zero area. Each wedge is integrated with its own profile. The independent analytic integrator also preserves disjoint vertical intervals instead of replacing them with their enclosing range. Neither repair changes an equality guard or widens the 1e-6 current tolerance.

Wall contact resolved when the fixture wall is rebuilt at one panel per cell pitch

Node cca-wall-at-cell-pitch, benchmark benchmarks/wall_at_cell_pitch.py (commits 2d327477, 840834b9, 26461a6a), figure and report at 8a666b14, 2026-09-15. With the production contact read at the polyline tangency to sub-micron accuracy (three-node quadratic in arc length), the remaining limited-row contact error is the sagitta of the fixture wall polyline against the true limiter, first order in panel length. This node re-sampled the wall at one, half and a quarter outboard panel per realised cell pitch (odd counts) beside the fixed 121-node baseline, on the weak and moderate analytic rows at 1000 and 2500 requested cells, and recorded contact position error against the analytic outboard tangency, level error in span, machine build wall time split (plasma and wall blocks), interaction-matrix bytes and the wall panel length over pitch. Both cell counts ran CPU on all_debug with the persistent compilation cache (jobs 1271206 and 1271237); the 2500 job was cut short by a serve restart after the weak group landed, leaving the moderate 2500 group with its 121-node baseline only (13 of 16 rows), noted per row and in the extrapolation caveat rather than re-measured.

Verdict: the polyline sagitta is the contact error and needs a curved wall representation at all practical counts. The measured error/pitch per panel/pitch slope is 0.475 on every row, and the error falls linearly with panel length (first order). One thousandth of the cell pitch — the position accuracy the clip needs — would therefore require roughly 57 000 wall nodes at 1000 cells and 91 000 at 2500 (the per-count figures: weak 1000 needs 57 275 at ~2950 s build, ~1.47 GB wall family; weak 2500 needs 90 561 at ~10 750 s build, ~5.67 GB; moderate 1000 needs 56 927 at ~2990 s, ~1.46 GB; moderate 2500 needs 89 957 from the fixed baseline, ~5.66 GB). The contact error falls with the panel over pitch — 0.474 of the pitch at one panel per pitch, 0.237 at half, 0.119 at a quarter — tracking the first-order slope to the resolution sampled, so no practical polyline count reaches one thousandth of pitch and the wall must be represented as a periodic spline with the tangency taken on the curve. Parts, receipts and the extrapolation table are under ~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/nova/s19-review/wall-pitch/.

Correction (lead ruling, 2026-09-15): the verdict above is withdrawn. Machine descriptions never carry a curved wall; every first wall is straight segments, so a periodic-spline wall is not a fix for anything the solver reads. The first-order contact error measured here is the Solov'ev oracle fixture comparing two different references: the analytic tangency is taken against the continuum limiter curve while the machine the fixture builds samples that curve into a 121-node polyline. The 0.47 pitch at one panel per pitch is the distance between those two references, and it vanishes when the oracle's contact reference is the flux extremum over the same polyline the solver sees. The low-field-side error that matters on these rows is the current allocation blowing up in the cells where the psi contours close near the outboard wall, which is the shadowed-carrier defect recorded under the limited-shadow root cause. The measurement and its parts stand as a characterisation of the fixture; no node follows.

Limited-row residual shadow: carrier root cause and terminal re-solves

Root cause. At revision 3082be61, the persisted weak 2500-cell terminal state is limited (one O candidate, zero X candidates), yet the connectivity flood labels 54 wall-cut, closed carriers PRIVATE_FLUX. The residual then copies those 54 carriers through unchanged. They alone contain 44.1144374851 Wb of physical-map disagreement; the other 8955 carriers agree to 2.2737367544e-13 Wb. This is not a state-only artefact: the analytic flux sampled at the same nodes also yields 40 provisional private carriers at 2500 cells and 39 at 1000 cells. The complete carrier census records index, R, Z, provisional domain, normalised flux, connectivity component and wall-polygon distance in docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/limited-shadow/receipt.json.

Physical rule and result. classify_domains at nova/equilibrium/domain.py:208-218 still exposes the raw diagnostic split. saddle_qualified_domains at domain.py:221-242, applied by the fixed-design read and finite-candidate predicate at forward_operator.py:1870-1915 and defended again by the residual-shadow builder at forward_operator.py:2549-2577, states the physical rule: connectivity disconnection is insufficient evidence for private flux. A finite qualified saddle candidate inside the wall — finite x_point and finite x_point_flux — retains the private labels regardless of which boundary class the read currently selects. Only a read with no finite saddle relabels provisional PRIVATE_FLUX carriers CORE. On weak terminal/analytic flux, the provisional counts are 64/39 at 1000 cells and 54/40 at 2500, while every qualified private count and flood-shadow count is zero. All four limited null censuses admit exactly one extremum and zero saddles; the single-null control retains eight physical private carriers behind its one admitted saddle.

Interpretation. A converged whole-cell row is a self-consistent fixed point and is not an oracle match until its difference panel is at the roundoff floor. Those are discretisation errors the exact clip must remove. By contrast, the single-null control is 1.55e-14 of span at maximum and is within one hundred times the 1e-14 roundoff floor.

The machine-readable table and input hashes are in docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/limited-shadow/oracle-overlay-error-receipt.json; the human report and accepted job log are under ~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/nova/s19-handoff/oracle-overlay/. The receipt pins the PNG SHA-256, the twelve analytic contour levels per row, every visible fixed difference level, the outboard chord extent and maximum, the roundoff-floor source, and the glob discovery census.

CPU test-lane backend abort: attributed to process-cumulative in-process compilation

Question. One pytest process over the forward-operator importers (observation, stencil_mesh, clip_quadrature, forward_operator and the constraint-protocol module) dies with SIGABRT (exit 134) inside the JAX CPU backend, on both arms of the delta gate, before pytest can report — so no failure ids are collected and every delta over this surface was unmeasured. The closing node attributes it from three cache treatments of one fixed six-module prefix in jax/jaxlib 0.11.0 (XLA client API 477, runtime pjrt_ifrt, python 3.14.2, pytest 9.1.1, JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu, x64 enabled, PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1, one all_debug job each).

casecache treatmentjobrcwallresult
Apersistent cache ON, warm shared home cache12713990454 s41 passed (pair 30 passed)
Bcache genuinely OFF (jax_enable_compilation_cache=False)12714371341956 sSIGABRT at test 40/41
Ccache ON, fresh EMPTY root via NOVA_FORWARD_COMPILATION_CACHE_ROOT12715261342041 sSIGABRT at test 40/41

All three land on the same terminal forward-solve test, tests/test_equilibrium_constraint_protocol.py::test_eliminated_constraint_reports_no_root_and_refuses_multiple_rows (41st in A and passes; 40th in B and C, where the process dies compiling it). The crash frame tracks whether that Nth program is a cache hit or a compile: a cache HIT load dies in compilation_cache.py:352 get_executable_and_time under compiler.py:768 _cache_read (repro sites: the earlier prefix_5 run, job 1271081, and the constraints base/after lanes, test_reduced_newton_constraints.py::test_a_traced_target_decides_what_a_captured_one_decides, which abort identically so the abort is not a regression of the changed lane's code); a cache MISS or cache OFF dies in compiler.py:350 backend_compile_and_load under compiler.py:729 _compile_and_write_cache (cases B and C), the forward solves reached through jax/_src/lax/control_flow/loops.py scan/fori_loop from nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py, with the C stack raise <- abort <- libjax_common.so.

Attribution. The on-disk persistent cache is neither the cause nor a necessary condition. Cache-off (B) and fresh-empty-cache-on (C) both force every program to compile in-process and both abort at the same terminal test; a warm shared cache (A) makes the process LOAD most programs instead of compiling them, so it never reaches the fatal state and the same test passes. The leading candidate is process-cumulative in-process compilation — an XLA / LLVM CPU resource exhausted after roughly fifty compiled large while_loop/fori_loop (pjit) programs in one process — with the crash frame wherever the next big program is materialised. The exit code 134 within a single aborting module is a property of running the forward-operator surface in one process, not of any module's code.

Fix it implies. Operational, not source: the standing gate stays the per-module fresh-process lane (one forward-operator module per process, so an abort costs one module, names it, and lets the others be measured); the persistent cache stays ON for speed but is not a correctness guard against the abort; and the upstream report to jax-ml/jax carries a minimal reproduction — nova's terminal protocol forward-solve test run after the rest of the prefix in one process, or a synthetic loop compiling roughly fifty large jit/while_loop graphs in a fresh process until abort — documenting that the crash frame tracks cache hit versus compile. No source file was changed by the closing node; the full record with per-case last Python frames and versions is the closing record in the s19-handoff cpu-abort report under ~/.config/reckon/crew/reports.

Exact-clip low state: a seed-selected second fixed point

Question. The weak 300-cell exact-clip solve converged with axis flux 46.66 Wb against the 49.96 Wb analytic value even though the weak 110-cell row matched the oracle. One H200 job tested four arms on both rows: production iteration from the analytic flux; the repaired-seed reference state; a rigid translation of the analytic flux by the reference state's axis error; and a per-cell booked-versus-analytic current census over the same clipped polygons. Job 1271758 completed both rows in 58 minutes with exit zero and the receipt marker LOW_STATE_EXIT rows=2 completed=True.

Fixed-point and displacement discriminator
requested cellsanalytic-start residualanalytic-start max difference / spananalytic-start axis fluxseed-start residualseed-start axis fluxchanged participation cellsreading
1103.666e-131.135e-449.942887 Wb3.420e-1349.942887 Wb0oracle-near positive control
3009.305e-141.080e-449.952060 Wb2.079e-1346.664612 Wb25seed-selected second fixed point

Arm A: the analytic state stays fixed. At both cell counts the analytic start converged after one production trip. Its states after 1, 2 and 4 trips are unchanged. At 300 cells the terminal residual is 9.305e-14 and the maximum solved-minus-analytic difference is 1.080e-4 of span, while the repaired seed separately converges at 2.079e-13 with axis flux 46.664612 Wb. A wrong map at the analytic state is therefore ruled out: the discrete map carries two converged fixed points on the 300-cell mesh.

Arm C: displacement explains most of the boundary offset. Rigidly translating the analytic flux by the low state's measured 33.2 mm axis displacement changes the production limiter level by 2.319 Wb, against the low state's 2.022 Wb offset. The remaining 0.297 Wb mismatch is 14.7 percent of the low-state offset, so rigid displacement explains 85.3 percent. This names the geometry of the second state; it does not make that state unique because arm A retains the oracle under the same exterior.

Arm D: the 428 kA difference is a class exchange, not missing current. Twenty-five cells change participation class between the analytic and low states. Against the analytically clipped fixture current grouped by terminal class, cut cells book 427,983 A more and whole cells book 427,632 A less; inactive cells differ by -143 A and the all-class remainder is 207 A. The low state moves the support boundary and redistributes current between whole and cut cells while retaining the target current.

Conclusion and consequence. The arms jointly support a seed-selected second self-consistent state. Two fixed points with the same target current and exterior mean the fixture exterior holds plasma position weakly. The operational defect is seed-basin selection. The next measurement is positional stiffness: apply one production map to analytic states rigidly translated from 0 to 60 mm and measure residual against displacement, exposing the width and curvature of the weak restoring basin without iteration-history ambiguity.

Fixture positional stiffness: the re-posed exterior is locally runaway

Measured 2026-09-16 in one H200 job. Job 1271814 used one card, eight cores and 128 GiB, completed all 84 requested displacement receipts in 728 seconds, and exited zero. On weak 110, weak 300 and moderate 300, the analytic flux was rigidly displaced by 0, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 and 60 mm separately outboard and vertically. The target current and each arm's exterior stayed fixed. One target-normalised production map and four successive trips of that same map were persisted for the analytic-clipped exterior and the former whole-cell exterior.

Verdict. The fixture exterior does not hold the plasma position. Every nonzero analytic-clipped displacement grows after four map trips rather than contracting. Five of the six fitted residual valleys remain below the low state's 8.6e-2-of-span separation at its 36 mm marker; the two moderate directions do not rescue the verdict because the axis itself still runs away. The former whole-cell posing is worse as a reference: its zero displacement rms floor is already 0.21 to 0.22 of span, and its outboard residual decreases under displacement. The two fixed points are therefore a weakly held positional basin, not a certificate that can be trusted from seed independence.

Re-posing that preserves the oracle. Retain the non-vacuum analytic construction and build an exterior family from the analytic total minus analytically clipped plasma images at nearby rigid displacements. Its first and second displacement derivatives provide an explicit restoring Taylor term while the undisplaced member remains the analytic oracle. A vacuum coil set fitted to the boundary is not an alternative: the Solovev exterior is not a vacuum field, so that fit would discard the oracle.

Exact-clip solve memory: reproduced, reduced, and held on correctness

Reproduction. One foreground all_debug CPU job (1271480, eight cores, 256 GiB, JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu, TMPDIR=/tmp in submission and payload) compiled the production exact-clip solve without executing it. XLA reported 25.465671, 51.807054 and 70.405273 GiB of temporaries at 135, 342 and 555 realised cells. Every rung contains nine pred[cells,cells] signatures, whose bytes grow with exponent exactly 2.0. Optimized HLO places the family inside jvp(compact_clipped_current_moments)/while: the cut-cell scan closed over the complete per-cell flux polynomial, so its differentiation carried one row for every cut-bank entry against every carried cell. The authored producer is ForwardFluxOperator.support_current_moments in nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py.

Implementation and corrected attribution. Commit 826358aa gives each compact cut polygon only its own flux polynomial and vectorizes that one-cell integration before scattering the three current moments back to the original carrier. This removed all nine pairwise predicates but did not reduce total solve memory: jobs 1271733 and 1271751 still measured 25.568408, 52.050680 and 70.773622 GiB at 135, 342 and 555 realised cells. The dominant retained workspace was instead the repeated f64[bank,12,cells,129,7] spline-level evaluation in ForwardFluxOperator._profile_support and _polished_level_root in nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py: 24 edge slots differentiated through twelve polish steps. Commits 9693713b through 9fa332fe retain the byte-identical full primal behind a custom-JVP boundary; the final measured arm rematerializes the exact bounded twelve-step derivative rather than retaining every polish intermediate.

The bounded twelve-step replay is 2.209e-8 to 1.042e-6 on those isolated roots, and the earlier complete-map measurement remains 7.877e-3 to 8.223e-3. The implicit arc tracer becomes an explicit parameter

The level-root arc tracer is now an argument of _traced_clip and of AtomicCellMesh.traced_clip, appended after every existing parameter and resolved at call time to the module's own twelve-step _traced_level_arc when it is None. The scan body calls tracer(...) instead of the module global, so a caller that needs a different derivative — an implicit-function tangent, for instance — passes its tracer explicitly rather than rebinding a module global through a patched __globals__ dictionary. That patched-dictionary clone is what this seam exists to replace; the seam is landed here, the clone deletion is not, because the clone lives outside this change's write scope.

What changed. Commit 935589ac: three hunks and sixteen lines in nova/equilibrium/separatrix_clip.py — the parameter, one docstring paragraph, a call-time alias, and the call site inside the gap-scan body. No numeric path changed, nothing inside _traced_level_arc changed, and because the parameter is appended last no existing positional caller shifts. On the default route the callee is the same function object, so the arithmetic of every existing route is unchanged by construction. tests/test_equilibrium_separatrix_clip.py gains one guard in 63 added lines.

Evidence that could have failed. The clone route and an explicit implicit tracer were driven over the same sixteen-cell mesh and agree on the clipped support: vertex-count sum 1584, total clipped area 12.566335557375638, support-vertex digest 99674cf594df2e543c2e93c0fe4b6e17270c1e03db3d9d3d04bb061659b3efda. The same receipt does not distinguish the tracers: its three arms agree on every figure, so it says nothing about whether the parameter is live, and the independent review of this run scored the liveness claim down for that reason. Liveness rests on the guard alone. The new guard counts tracer invocations at trace time, which jax.lax.scan makes possible, and reads 0 under a temporary mutation that ignores arc_tracer; the mutation was reverted before the commit. Receipts: reports/nova/s19-local/arc-tracer/arc-tracer-equivalence.json and …/logs.

Importer gate. What changed. Three commits on the node: 294b070e deletes eight lines of clone construction and one alias and rewrites the exact-support call; aa2eec1a and dbf411d9 add tests/test_equilibrium_forward_operator.py, which pins the route and the absence of a clone.

Evidence - the moments are identical, not merely close. Receipt reports/nova/s19-local/arc-tracer-clone/clone-deletion-moments.json drives the weak-rotation-reactor -110 certificate machine and its exact state in a fresh CPU process per arm, one arm on the node head and one on the main checkout, and records the exact-clip per-cell support moments the forward operator raises on its own accord. Max absolute difference is exactly 0.0 on every array - clipped area, first area moment, second area moment, per-cell vertex count, the support-vertex table and the cell currents - over 135 cells of which 121 are clipped, with both shapes, the dtype and a sha256 digest printed per array.

Why that zero is a measurement and not a blank. Five ways the instrument is shown live, each reported in the receipt:

  • The recorder fired; an arm whose recorder records nothing exits non-zero rather than reporting an empty comparison.
  • The exact and chord modes of the same arm disagree - exact total area 21.20135866955972 against chord 23.893661380085774 - so the exact clip was exercised rather than short-circuited into a shared code path.
  • A one-ulp perturbation of the area array is detected as different, so the equality test resolves the smallest representable difference.
  • The head module reports no _implicit_clip_globals and no clone function in its namespace while the base arm reports both, so the two arms are not both running post-change code.
  • The base arm is the main checkout, and the two modules the change touches are byte-identical between the orientation base revision 26c45542 and that checkout's HEAD, established by an empty git diff --name-only over exactly those two paths.

Tests. One module per fresh CPU process, each in its own all_debug job, root venv interpreter, JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu: tests/test_equilibrium_separatrix_clip.py 23 passed in 60.5 s; tests/test_equilibrium_forward_operator.py 3 passed in 113.3 s.

The guard is falsifiable in two directions. The clone detector is first run on a synthetic patched-globals clone of the traced clip built inside the test and must flag it, so a green detector that never fires fails rather than passes; and the tracer spy asserts that every traced clip call the exact mode raises carries arc_tracer is _implicit_traced_level_arc, while the committed chord mode raises no traced clip call at all as the negative side of the same assertion.

Narrowing during the node. The detector first keyed on the deleted names, which would not survive a rename, and an over-broad version flagged two functions legitimately defined in clip_quadrature. It now tests the structural signature: a module attribute that is a function whose __globals__ reports the clip module's __name__ while not being that module's own dictionary. Importing a function from the clip cannot produce that signature; carrying a copy of its namespace can, which is what the removed clone did.

Scope defect carried. tests/test_exact_clip_memory.py imports the deleted name at line 24, rebinds _traced_level_arc inside its __globals__ at line 81 and calls the clone at line 450, so that module now fails at import; it lies outside this node's write scope and needs a node of its own. benchmarks/exact_clip_memory_scaling.py line 498 uses _implicit_traced_level_arc, which is retained and unaffected.

No terminal forward state is produced by this node, so this record carries no poloidal flux contour panel: the evidence is a per-cell moment table with its controls, over the same clipped geometry already drawn in the exact-clip records above.

The typed census saddle reaches the production spline-chain clip, and the independent measure that was to confirm it is wrong

Landed 2026-09-20 in commit d90a522fe on base 05aafeae5. The production forward operator passed no saddle vertex to the spline-chain clip, so the operator's own branch expansion was discarded and no production solve split the X-point cell. The profile support now supplies the typed census saddle as the clip's saddle vertex — topology.x_point — and a supplied saddle that is not finite admits no expansion, so an absent census saddle refuses the cell and packs an empty inclusion rather than NaN geometry. The refusal is what the second committed case pins: with a non-finite supplied saddle the cell is refused, its inclusion empty and its area and vertex count zero, while the branch arrays stay finite.

What is established is the plumbing. The forward operator passes the typed census saddle to the spline-chain clip, and the focused gate is twelve tests with two added and none failing, so the route from the census read into the clip is pinned. What remains unverified is the numerical agreement with an independent oracle, not the route through the operator; the red gate below says nothing against the clip.

The localisation is the node's deliverable and the repair list for the next reconstruction. Four defects, in the order they are met when rebuilding the region measure: (1) the reconstructed sectors wind clockwise; (2) one sector spans 2.05e-02 square metres against a cell interior far smaller than that; (3) the two sectors it labels confined (5.09e-04 and 1.91e-03 m2) are not the carrier's core and private-flux wedges (5.72e-04 and 4.19e-03 m2); (4) the core it selects by centroid projection along the axis direction is the quad above the saddle, where the carrier's core is the quad beside it. The polygon sets differ outright, so a mislabelled or mis-paired region is the fault and not a quadrature tolerance.

The certificate re-solve half of the section fence was deferred by the brief and not attempted, so its absence is a deferred clause rather than a failure.

The gate is red, and it reddens on the instrument. One all_debug allocation (8 cpus, 64G, TMPDIR=/tmp in the submit environment and in the payload, uv never invoked on the compute node) ran 110, 300 and 500 cells in one job and stopped at the first row: core-side current relative error 1.388e-01 against the 1e-13 limit, receipt at docs/figures/cut-cell-current-attribution/oracle/receipt.json. The comparison above shows why that is not evidence about the clip. The carrier's four wedge areas are 5.72e-04, 4.19e-03, 1.76e-02 and 5.36e-04 m2; the reconstruction's four sectors are 2.05e-02, 5.09e-04, 6.38e-05 and 1.91e-03 m2, all clockwise, one of them spanning more than the cell interior admits. The two sectors it labels confined are not the carrier's core and private-flux wedges, and its core selection by centroid projection along the axis direction picks the quad above the saddle while the carrier's core is the quad beside it. The pairing of exact edge roots into regions is therefore wrong in the reconstruction, and the next node owns that pairing.

Independent oracle: the cell frame repair

The independent wedge oracle reconstructed sectors against the cell polygon as the machine exposes it, while the atomic mesh stores every cell in the counter-clockwise traversal _normalise_cells produces. A separatrix root is encoded as an edge index plus a fraction along that edge, so the two frames name different boundary segments: each solved root was consumed on the wrong edge and the sectors joined roots across the wrong branch. The recorded X-point cell at 110 requested cells has signed area -2.293827560763972e-02 m2, so it is one of the reversed cells. Indexing the supplied fractions against the normalised polygon reproduces the exact roots, so the root-finding pair is not at fault and the pairing rule itself is correct.

Certificate trip stall: fixed quadrature, zero tangent, finite current jumps

Measured 2026-09-21; both requested rows reproduced. The certificate rows stall at a current-quadrature threshold, followed by globalization refusal and active-set settlement. The committed chord path supplies whole atomic polygons; pointwise confinement on fixed quadrature points makes the static-profile current moments piecewise constant as the flux moves. The local automatic derivative cannot carry a boundary point crossing. This is a discontinuous current-support map, not an outer residual-shadow cycle. The analytic state also has a separate, much smaller nonzero discrete map defect; its amplitude is near unity, so the seed's factor-two amplitude does not prove a global profile-normalization inconsistency.

What stops the rows

The coarse row accepts 15 of 30 Newton proposals across the three trips; the fine row accepts 11 of 30. Each terminal trip refuses all ten proposals with sufficient_decrease_refused, although the Krylov actions qualify (linear residual reductions 2.2141e-16 and 4.5909e-16 against 1e-5). The proposed step maxima are 5.924467474 and 5.629719016 Wb; applied factors are zero. Continuation, model rebuild and descent do not promote another state.

Every trip has zero residual-shadow difference and no cycle damping. Eight coarse and seven fine cells change nonzero-current membership in the first trip, then none. All cell currents are bit-identical from trip one onward. The next field moves are 7.7383e-7 and 1.0000e-7 Wb; the third trip repeats the second exactly. Outboard-band current stays at 1.018229 MA coarse and 0.805127 MA fine. This is settlement, not an outer active-set cycle or exhausted trip budget.

A local tangent that cannot see a quadrature crossing

On the 135-cell terminal state, the map JVP along its own 5.924467474 Wb defect is exactly zero. Differentiating the map plus the identity recovers the nonzero direction with zero error, so the instrument sees a known-present tangent. At factor 1e-10 along that direction, the image is unchanged. At 1e-8, 1e-6 and 1e-4, cell 66 loses exactly 847.4318788 A and the image jumps 0.02419419492 Wb. That cell is inboard, at (4.902912181, 1.502453181) m, with confined quadrature fraction 0.1281023672 and initial current 19556.1682658 A. The profile's psi_norm > 1 Boolean selector on whole-cell quadrature is the discontinuous operation; the static profile has no continuous flux dependence between those crossings.

A full defect step reduces the sup residual to 0.05653431145; a half step reduces it to 0.05371145764. Thus not every candidate is uphill in the reported norm. The production admission also uses an eighth-norm merit and model trust. The receipt proves the combined refusal, while the exact rejecting subcriterion was not decomposed: an optional extension was cancelled at allocation completion. The completed finite-difference evidence establishes the blind local model and the current jumps; it does not justify weakening the guard.

The four required alternatives

  • A factor-two pin excludes the analytic equilibrium: refuted as stated. Analytic amplitudes are 0.9997620365 and 1.0000712417. The seed/stall amplitude near two is compensation for a wrong current-support state.
  • An outboard outer-mask cycle: refuted on both captured traces. Shadow masks never change and returned cell currents cease changing after trip one.
  • The seed only needs more trips: the seed is far away, but three of sixteen trips end in settlement. The unused budget is not the stopping cause.
  • Residual is mask oscillation: independent map applications reproduce every residual on the unchanged masks. It is a fixed-point defect, not an analytic-distance metric; its terminal absolute values remain 5.92447 and 5.62972 Wb.

The analytic state is still not an exact discrete fixed point

Pinned analytic one-map residuals are 0.001074741678 and 0.0007424374321, with changes 0.05339129072 and 0.03706688786 Wb. Unpinned residuals are 0.001288052777 and 0.0008950247864. All exceed the locked 1e-12 bound; removing the pin does not close the analytic consistency error. Its allocation, coupling and topology-read shares remain to be measured separately. The axis-read error already present on exact sampled flux is 15.123 and 3.219 mm.

Current terms, norm composition and coupling

For the historical full analytic step, the predicted eighth-norm numerator is 39.9193900 Wb versus actual 0.00740588401 Wb; the denominator is 114.687317 Wb versus 76.9303399 Wb. The map prediction error is 23.8329617 Wb. Its zeroth-current, radial-coefficient and vertical-coefficient contributions have maxima 22.0682811, 1.59475204 and 2.49452272 Wb; their signed sum reconstructs the map error to 9.24e-14 Wb. Per-cell unnormalised and pinned current errors reach 184595.824 A and 395986.101 A. These maxima are not additive: their locations and signs differ.

On the authoritative 135-cell full analytic step, the numerator is predicted 27.9129853 versus actual 0.00740588401 Wb, a factor 3769.03. The denominator is 102.981126 versus 76.9303399 Wb, only 1.33863 times, reducing the merit error to 2815.59 times. On 342 cells those factors are 5326.23 and 1.38297, leaving 3851.30 times. Substituting the actual numerator into the predicted denominator gives 7.19150e-5 and 5.48145e-5; substituting only the actual denominator leaves 0.362835 and 0.403764. The eighth norm is applying the wrong predicted residual, not creating a three-order discrepancy from an accurate flux prediction.

The authoritative current error is dominated by the zeroth-current image: maxima 17.3127758 / 18.8602119 Wb (135 / 342). Radial coefficients contribute 0.752220 / 0.916077 Wb and vertical coefficients 1.528222 / 1.202314 Wb. Their signed sums reproduce the full analytic map error, 16.5949356 / 19.0191689 Wb, to 8.88e-14 / 1.12e-13 Wb. Thus neither a nonlinear coupling nor a changed residual shadow is needed to explain either full analytic refusal.

Normalising the linear raw-current prediction separates two signed contributions: raw-current curvature gives 22.9427581 / 25.4497374 Wb, and scalar-current-pin curvature gives 6.39020497 / 6.46293651 Wb, with partial cancellation. The predicted raw totals are 12.586408 / 12.215064 MA against actual 16.313610 / 16.314423 MA. Both pinned actual and predicted totals remain 16.3147733118 MA: the failure is the distribution, despite the correct total.

The full-step raw-current error maxima are 202707.613 / 122247.309 A; pinned maxima are 417127.383 / 246693.907 A. Coarse cell 15 is actually 169840.381 A but predicted 586967.764 A, and fine cell 255 is actually 61252.1084 A but predicted 307946.015 A. Neither changes its centroid classification: continuous support motion and the common pin affect even cells whose labels do not flip. On coarse cells, 5.06052 MA of the raw L1 error is in cells whose confined label changes, 2.08293 MA in cells whose label does not; on fine cells, 6.27503 and 1.31350 MA respectively. The cellwise vectors and ranked examples are retained in the receipts.

Large Newton moves can additionally change residual shadows. Coarse half-Newton flips eleven shadow entries and leaves a 62.1862 Wb remainder in the unshadowed coupling identity; fine full-Newton and quarter-Newton flip thirteen and five entries, with remainders 88.3279 and 50.7089 Wb. These are not evidence that the fixed coupling became nonlinear: the instrument's plain e + C N identity omits the candidate's copy-through shadow term. They are explicitly branch-changing candidates and already fail actual sufficient decrease. The full analytic candidates have zero shadow flips and close that identity at rounding precision.

What the mechanism tests establish and leave unresolved

The historical analytic direction flips 63 confined/open centroid classifications. The authoritative full analytic directions flip 49 and 129; their nonzero-current supports change in 47 and 130 cells. The branch at the candidate therefore differs materially from that at the linearization point. This establishes extrapolation across branch changes, not a stale or incorrectly selected base branch.

For the historical witness, the analytic JVP agrees with a central finite difference at fraction increment 1e-6 to relative error 1.6794e-9. Its second directional derivative, measured from JVP differences, is 34.995898 Wb per squared fraction at the origin and 113.494946 at the full analytic endpoint; increments 1e-4 and 1e-5 agree in the shown digits. At the authoritative coarse terminal, the analytic and Newton JVP errors are 1.13064e-9 and 2.11781e-10. Along the coarse analytic ladder, second directional maxima at fractions 0.001, 0.0625, 0.5 and 1 are 24.89098, 31.29904, 59.35442 and 71.91993 Wb per squared fraction. Each local curvature pair has zero confined-label flips, and its two increments agree closely. Thus smooth within-branch curvature is present as well as the many full-path label changes; a label-flip-only explanation is insufficient.

The fine terminal does NOT pass that local tangent check. Central finite-difference discrepancies at increment 1e-6 are 0.999565 (analytic), 0.995716 (Newton) and 1.000092 (map defect). They are measured failures, not rounded passes. At fine analytic fractions 0.001 and 0.5, the JVP-difference curvature is stable at 59.0121 and 91.1154 Wb per squared fraction. At the full analytic endpoint it changes from 331.316 to 290.285 when the increment shrinks from 1e-4 to 1e-5, despite zero local centroid-label flips. Fine Newton at fraction 0.125 changes from 73440.1 to 1885.06. Those estimates are not converged second derivatives. The origin finite-difference endpoint states were not retained, so the receipt cannot attribute its mismatch to a particular root, topology read or subcell quadrature transition. A branch-resolved tangent audit is a required follow-on; a corrected-linearization repair on this row is not ruled out.

The classification detector sees a deliberately flipped bit (count one) and each current detector sees nonzero support. The same detector records one local confined flip in each fine Newton curvature pair at fraction 0.0625. This is a physical positive control for the zero local counts elsewhere. The moment-image JVP identities agree to 3.55e-15 / 2.84e-14 Wb or better on both rows; that verifies the decomposition's arithmetic, not the differentiability of the nonlinear map.

Repair supported by the measured refusal; convergence acceptance unchanged

Implement actual-candidate acceptance for a pessimistic model: keep finite checks, merit <= incumbent_merit * (1 - 1e-4 * fraction), and strict own-mask sup-residual decrease. If those actual tests pass and predicted decrease is nonpositive, promote the measured candidate while marking the model unreliable and rebuilding it for future proposals. When predicted decrease is positive, the existing realized-versus-predicted decrease check can remain. Do not replace the actual merit with the predicted merit, relax the sufficient-decrease slope, alter the current pin or increase the budgets.

The direct falsifiable acceptance for that refusal repair is that the historical full analytic witness and both authoritative full analytic candidates pass the candidate selector, while every actually worsening Newton candidate in this measured ladder remains refused. The historical half-defect acceptance must remain. Curvature-aware trust radii may prevent a large bad Newton proposal, but shrinking the sampled analytic direction rejects every tested fraction below one and cannot alone recover this witness.

This is not proof of a complete convergence repair. All seven sampled Newton fractions increase actual merit on both terminals. The production qualified Newton solves are well resolved (achieved linear-residual ratios 2.30e-13 and 1.93e-13) but their full nonlinear merits are 0.601744 and 1.301857, against model predictions 1.33e-14 and 1.63e-14. The analytic candidate itself has sup residual 9.53950e-5 / 9.59627e-5, still above the locked 1e-12 bound, and is labelled converged=false in the panel.

Cold-seed acceptance remains locked on BOTH rows: converged=true, sup residual <= 1e-12, analytic axis and every admitted X-point inside one characteristic pitch (0.4660634103582032 / 0.28221540988057975 m), and the joint null qualification. Retain per-trip shared-level contours, both null sets and the wall; neither row may be dropped. Keep sixteen outer trips, ten Newton steps, thirty Krylov iterations, sufficient decrease and the current pin unchanged. The separately dispatched merged-head verification owns that acceptance. This investigation leaves the driving followup and all plan status fields unchanged.

The flipping cells are 128, 156 and 255 in every straddling row and every direction, and their open and label masks flip with their confined mask; no shadow flag flips. The nonzero-current support is 177 cells and is identical at the plus and minus endpoints and against the base at every row, so the flip changes moment values rather than the support: the raw current total moves from 9.20315e6 A to 9.18517e6 A (0.195 percent) while individual cells move 1.2 to 2.0 percent, the largest being cell 255 at 29902.1 / 29902.3 / 29315.9 A. Every named carrier — cells 255, 51, 43, 256, 284 and 44 at increment 1e-6 — is wholly inside at the base and at both endpoints. The flux jump is largest at grid nodes 1065, 181, 1064 and 1060.

Which root it is. On the analytic direction the flip vanishes at a smaller increment: at 1e-8 there are no flips, the implied jump collapses to 7.5e-6, the fd-to-jvp ratio is 1.00000 and the residual discrepancy is 2.5e-7, so the base state lies between 1e-8 and 1e-7 of the step from that surface. On the Newton and map-defect directions the flips persist and the ratio grows as exactly 1/h with no limit, so the state sits on the surface. A wrong local coefficient is excluded by two facts: a coefficient defect would drive fd/jvp to a finite value while these ratios grow one decade per decade of increment, and the implied jump is the same constant 1.629 to 1.700 across four decades and all three directions whose jvp norms differ 38-fold, which a direction-dependent coefficient error cannot produce. Positive controls: the reproduction above, a seeded single-bit flip counted as 1, 177 nonzero-current cells counted, the 1e-4 control reporting the same three flips and jump, and the clean 1e-8 rung reporting a per-cell current gap of 0.0026 A against a 6.26e4 A difference. Attempt 1 (job 1275517) failed in 51 s on an argument-count defect in the driver itself and measured nothing; its log is preserved in the reports directory.

This corroborates the merit ladder's mechanism — the linear model predicts the analytic candidate's merit to 1.00023 while no classification flip occurs and is wrong by 3851x with 129 flips — and supports a step that stays inside a branch, a branch-frozen linearisation re-classifying only at acceptance, or a continuation in the clip geometry, over any coefficient repair. The two flip counts are computed on different state pairs, so that agreement is an association rather than a cross-check. The 135-cell terminal passes the same instrument at 1.7e-9, which this audit does not revisit. Why the ring read misses, and the measured twin-loop alternative

Landed 2026-09-22 without a production or test-source change. On the analytic single-null flux at nine rungs from 132 to 2616 realised cells, the production ring-quadratic read again admits seven saddles and misses 132 and 340. The cell-centred own-node quadratic census admits 9 of 9; the vertex-centred dual census admits 8 of 9; their union admits 9 of 9. Newton polish of every union seed on the global tensor spline preserves 9-of-9 admission in three or four steps. The polished error spans 0.01395 to 0.04202 cell pitch, although polish is not uniformly more accurate than the best seed.

The proposed same-side mechanism explains 340 but not 132. At 340 cells the analytic X-point is 0.07088 pitch from the nearest cell boundary and the six containing-cell sides carry analytic separatrix root counts [1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 0]: two roots do share one side. At 132 cells the null is still closer, 0.03521 pitch, but the roots are [1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1], one each on four sides. In both cases the containing ring and every recorded neighbour ring have only two cyclic sign changes, so the production raw saddle population is zero. The cell candidates lie 0.06359 and 0.03137 pitch from the analytic saddle; their mode-ratio distances are 0.58095 and 0.48394 pitch, both pass the inside-or-near-source-cell and wall-containment checks, and the private-shadow filter does not apply to saddles. The four-change raw gate therefore explains both misses before mode, containment, wall or shadow filtering; a same-side double branch is the geometry behind only the 340-cell instance.

Recommendation for the generator implementation. Use the cell-centred own-node quadratic-root census: it alone admits 9 of 9, while the vertex-centred dual misses 132 and adds no admission on this sample. Pre-filter finite roots by a nonsingular indefinite Hessian, the existing inside-or-near-source-cell criterion and wall containment, then apply global-spline Newton polish only to the few typed and contained representatives. Keep the four-change count as a diagnostic rather than the admission gate, and keep the vertex loop as a diagnostic or fallback rather than the hot-path generator. The proposed cell generator costs 0.0370x to 0.0837x the production read on titan; the complete twin census plus polish is the conservative upper bound at 1.654x to 4.166x.

Program census and reduction choice

The exact 110 HLO carries 22,718 computations and 133,161,787 direct computation-protobuf bytes, against chord's 11,663 computations and 57,198,205 bytes. The GPU executable format does not embed the HLO module verbatim, so these are HLO computation bytes rather than a partition of GPU executable bytes. The largest exact source totals are Bernstein.binom 27,521,787 bytes, _monomial_antiderivative 11,987,303, _traced_clip 6,004,528, Bernstein.basis 5,380,953, _sampled_arc_polynomial_moments 4,183,836, Bernstein.coefficent_matrix 3,682,243, _cell_banked_current_moments 3,104,537 and clipped_support_current_moments 2,237,309. Chord carries only 5,805,033 bytes in _monomial_antiderivative, 2,602,449 in _traced_clip and 2,080,521 in _sampled_arc_polynomial_moments.

The largest named exact computations are region_215.9730 at 2,715,161 bytes, region_217.9728.clone.clone.clone at 955,241, region_3026.8169.clone.clone.clone at 757,826 led by _traced_clip, region_218.8540.clone.clone.clone at 571,843, and region_2528.5644.clone.clone.clone.clone.clone at 549,180. The concentration in exact polygon and moment algebra points first to lower clip and moment order through closed-form polygon moments. The near-doubling of computation count and repeated clip frames leave one vmapped per-cell clip body as the second reduction to measure. With no 300 exact HLO, this record does not invent a quantitative choice at the gate rung.

Exact-support deficit per cut cell: a fail-closed moment-bank overflow, not a geometry zero

Node cca-exact-support-deficit-per-cell-attribution, 2026-09-23, revision 1f85669c0. The weak 110-requested / 135-realised certificate row is censused in exact and chord mode at two fixed states — the production cold seed and the committed chord terminal state — in one all_debug job with JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu and TMPDIR=/tmp, the root interpreter run directly and uv never invoked on the compute node. Scope is the 135-realised row only.

The traced clip is finite while the exact current is undefined

At the terminal state (boundary level 10.3951318 Wb, polarity 1, 43 analytic cut cells) the traced support is healthy: area, full_area, the first and second area moments, contour_area, included and vertex_count are all finite, refused_cell_count is 4 and vertex_capacity is 158. The exact-mode current is nonetheless NaN for all 135 cells, so the named cause is not a geometry zero. Instrumenting every entry of nova.equilibrium.clip_quadrature.clipped_support_current_moments produces exactly one overflowing call:

cells=135  capacity=1  boundary_reduction=True  cut_count=2  overflow=True

This is the whole-cell branch of forward_operator._cell_banked_current_moments, which integrates the current with cut_cell_capacity=1, against the quadratic level-set boundary that clip_quadrature._flux_selected_current_moments re-derives and calls back in with at that inherited capacity. The quadratic level crosses two whole cells, so clipped_support_current_moments fails closed (jnp.where(overflow, jnp.nan, value)) and the entire exact-mode current field becomes undefined for every cell, cut or not. At the seed state (boundary level 35.8528226 Wb) the same call has cut_count=0, no overflow, and exact mode returns a finite current. The chord route is unaffected: it passes the full cut-cell bank capacity (135) and its boundary-reduction cut count (30 seed, 41 terminal) stays under it.
